permissions.summary: Linux desktop capture typically relies on session capabilities rather than OS privacy prompts.
Linux input control generally depends on session support instead of a centralized permission prompt.
Audio device access is usually mediated by the active audio stack and user session.

diagnostics.message: Wayland output `sunshine-headless` appears to be a simulated/headless display. In this class of session xdg-desktop-portal Screenshot can time out waiting for an access dialog and the grim fallback can hang, so Tendril does not advertise display capture for this target.
diagnostics.suggested_action: Use a Wayland session with a working screenshot portal/grim backend, or run automation against the packaged X11/Xvfb headless helper. Incorrect simulated refresh-rate metadata is a known caveat and is not itself treated as the failure.
